def: something heard, i.e. a sound, rumor, announcement; abstractly, audience
kjv: bruit, fame, hear(-ing), loud, report, speech, tidings.

occurrences.text: And it came to pass, when Laban heard the tidings of Jacob his sister’s son, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. And he told Laban all these things.
Thou shalt not raise a false report: put not thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness.
Now if thou shalt kill all this people as one man, then the nations which have heard the fame of thee will speak, saying,

This day will I begin to put the dread of thee and the fear of thee upon the nations that are under the whole heaven, who shall hear report of thee, and shall tremble, and be in anguish because of thee.
And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the Lord, she came to prove him with hard questions.

And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, she came to prove Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem, with a very great company, and camels that bare spices, and gold in abundance, and precious stones: and when she was come to Solomon, she communed with him of all that was in her heart.
Destruction and death say, We have heard the fame thereof with our ears.
I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.
As soon as they hear of me, they shall obey me: the strangers shall submit themselves unto me.
Praise him upon the loud cymbals: praise him upon the high sounding cymbals.
As at the report concerning Egypt, so shall they be sorely pained at the report of Tyre.

And I will set a sign among them, and I will send those that escape of them unto the nations, to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, that draw the bow, to Tubal, and Javan, to the isles afar off, that have not heard my fame, neither have seen my glory; and they shall declare my glory among the Gentiles.
Then Pharaoh’s army was come forth out of Egypt: and when the Chaldeans that besieged Jerusalem heard tidings of them, they departed from Jerusalem.
The king of Babylon hath heard the report of them, and his hands waxed feeble: anguish took hold of him, and pangs as of a woman in travail.
There is no healing of thy bruise; thy wound is grievous: all that hear the bruit of thee shall clap the hands over thee: for upon whom hath not thy wickedness passed continually?
O Lord, I have heard thy speech, and was afraid: O Lord, revive thy work in the midst of the years, in the midst of the years make known; in wrath remember mercy.
